nodes.title: Leather Care by KORDOVAN
nodes.body:
We use only the best leather, made to stand the test of time. Handcrafted by expert artisans all over the world, our leather goods deserve to be treated with care. Protect your investment with our specially formulated leather care products to ensure the lifetime of your leather collection. 

 

MAINTAINING YOUR LEATHER

Maintain your favorite leather pieces regularly to ensure soft and supple leather. Leather can be cleaned and restored with a regimen of leather care products designed to clean, condition and protect.

Leather Care can help maintain your product longer. We recommend conditioning your leather at a minimum of every 6 months. If you are in a dryer (hot or cold) climate please condition your product as soon as it feels less supple, dull or faded. Vegetable tanned leather when conditioned should feel slightly oiled and look rich. Similar to the nature of skin it needs to be moisturized as soon as it feels dry.

 

Tips & Tricks

 

- Never wash your leather bag in the washing machine.
- Keep cosmetics inside a pouch or small case. Cap all pens and anything that might leak on the leather.
- Avoid cleaning products with alcohol, turpentine or other mineral spirits. We recommend Will Leather Care products, specially formulated to extend the life and preserve the natural beauty of the leather.
- Store leather bags properly when not in use; keep out of direct sunlight and in low humidity as sunlight fades and dries leather.
- If leather gets wet, absorb as much water as possible with a thick hand towel and then air dry.

 

How To:

 

1. Leather is susceptible to absorbing grease and oils; handle with clean hands. Repeat every 6 months or as needed to clean, condition and protect leather goods from soiling and water spotting.
2. Apply a cleaner made specifically for the leather needing maintenance. We recommend using an All-In-One Leather Solution.
3.Using a soft cotton cloth, apply approximately 1 oz. of the solution all over the leather.
4. Allow the leather to dry for at least 12 hours away from sunlight and heat.
5. When dry, buff the leather with a soft cotton cloth using a circular motion.

CLEANING YOUR LEATHER


Fine leather deserves good care because even the best leather will dry and crack over time. If handled roughly or stored improperly, your leather goods may stain or prematurely deteriorate. Quality leather cleaners and conditioners preserve the character and extend the natural life of leather. Many of our bags are designed with bridle leather – top quality leather that has gone through an extensive tanning and finishing process; only the best quality hides free of flaws are selected. The final product is very soft and flexible, yet strong in its ability to withstand daily use. Quality bridle leather only gets better with proper cleaning and conditioning.



HOW TO ENHANCE THE NATURAL BEAUTY:


Use this method twice a year to clean and polish all fine smooth leathers.
- Dampen a soft cotton cloth with warm water.
- Using a circular motion, carefully clean the leather.
- Allow to dry for at least 11 hours away from direct sunlight and heat.
- Before completely dry, rub Saddle Oil all over the leather.
- If needed, apply a second coat within 30 minutes.
- Finish drying. How to Preserve Leather & Repel Water:
- Condition leather once a year to repel water and keep leather soft.
- Dampen a soft cotton cloth with warm water.
- Warm the leather with a hair dryer on low for 30 seconds
- Apply Mink Oil Crème, including the strap and all seams and stitching.
- Allow leather to dry for 12 hours away from sunlight and heat.
- Apply a second coat for additional weather protection.

 

REDUCING SCRATCHES & REMOVING SPOTS

 

It’s common for leather to get scratches and spots over time from normal use. Though it is difficult to truly repair leather because it is an organic material, there are several methods of minimizing the appearance of the damage with a little care. Your leather goods will patina before your very eyes – a reflection of the journey you’ve taken. A patina naturally develops in response to your environment and makes your bag one of a kind. The transformation in its coloring is a characteristic of quality leather and signifies its inherent beauty.

 

HOW TO REDUCE SCRATCHES:

 

- Leather is susceptible to absorbing grease and oils; handle with clean hands.
- Locate the scratch or spot on the leather goods
- Using the oils from your hands, bend and work the spot back and forth over the scratch and marks.
- Continue as needed working the leather. The scratch will continue to disappear over time.

 

HOW TO REMOVE SPOTS:

 

1. Remove spots as soon as they appear; don’t let it sit on the leather too long.

2. Use a baby wipe and fold it in half. Do not use wipes that contain alcohol, dyes or fragrance.

3. Place your hand on the opposite side of the stain and wipe away, cleaning the spot and surrounding area.

4. Rub with moderate pressure to remove the stain; using too much force may discolor the leather.

 

HOW TO CLEAN COTTON CANVAS, WOOL AND RAW SILK:


1. Using a soft-bristled brush, gently brush the canvas using a circular motion.

2. If spot remains, dab gently using a soft cotton cloth with warm water without any detergent.

3. Allow the spot to dry.

4. If spot still remains, use a mild detergent with a mild concentration (such as Woolite) and spot clean again; use a soft cotton cloth with the mild detergent solution and dab gently. Note: We recommend performing a test in a hidden place to ensure the detergent will not alter the color of the fabric.

5. If the spot still remains, please contact our Customer Service.

nodes.title: How to Choose the Perfect Leather Wallet for Men in 2024: A Complete Guide
nodes.body:
It's important to choose a good leather wallet that is both practical and unique. In 2024, Leather wallets are a top choice for many people because they are durable, and classic, and the way they develop character over time. When selecting a leather wallet, consider factors such as design, material quality, and functionality to ensure it meets your needs for everyday use, business, or special occasions. At Kordovan, we provide expert advice to help you find a high-quality leather wallet that suits your personal preferences and lifestyle.

Types of Men's Leather Wallets

Kordovan offers multiple types of leather wallets for men at online and in-store. We have a lot of designs and sizes that will suit every type of user, but it's important to first understand the different types of leather wallets to select one that fits your lifestyle and daily needs. Knowing the features and advantages of each type will help you select a wallet that meets your specific needs and complements your style.

Bi-Fold Wallets

Bi-fold wallets are classic and commonly used by men. Their smart and simple design makes them very popular. Bifolds have two sides that fold in half, making them compact enough to slip into your pocket without becoming bulky or uncomfortable. Cash can be placed in the rear pocket, while cards can be stored in the compartments on either side.

Smart Wallets

Smart wallets are designed for those who prefer to carry just a handful of essentials. It's small, light, and can easily fit in front pockets, making it perfect for those who don’t want to carry a lot of things.

Travel Wallets

Travel wallet offers a convenient way to store important things like passports, boarding passes, credit cards, and money. It's a great addition to your travel accessories, ideal for frequent travelers who prioritize convenience and security while on the go.

 

Card Holder Wallets

Card holder wallets are great for people who prefer to use cards instead of cash for a cash-free lifestyle. It's small, has many slots, and is good for people who don't need much space.

Money Clip Wallets

Money clip wallets are ideal for someone who primarily carries cash and a few cards but prefers not to carry a bulky wallet. It looks superior and people like them for the quick access to their money.

Zipper Wallets

Zipper wallets offer extra security and peace of mind due to their zippered closure. This feature makes them ideal for those who carry a mix of cards, cash, and coins.

 

Long Wallets

A long wallet is known for a checkbook wallet, this type of wallet is longer and usually used to carry many items. This wallet has lots of room for cards, money, and others essentials. It's a great choice for people who need to carry a lot.

RFID Wallets

RFID wallets are equipped with technology to prevent unauthorized scanning of your cards. This type is crucial for individuals who place a high value on security in their daily important stuff.

Tri-Fold Wallets

Tri-fold wallets are ideal for individuals who require additional storage,They feature three folds, with multiple compartments for card slots, bills, cash, and occasionally an ID window. This design makes them perfect for carrying a variety of essentials in a compact form.

Consider Your Needs and Lifestyle Before Choosing the Wallet

For Daily Use: A Wallet Fits for Your Routine and Preferences

When choosing a men's leather wallet for daily use, think about things that make everyday life easier. It's important to select pure leather that can resist regular use for the long term. A wallet that is easy to access and slim enough to not be hardy in your pocket. Think about how many spaces you need to keep your important things organized and easy to find throughout the day. A fine leather wallet should be both practical and stylish, so it can easily fit into your daily routine.

For Travel: Keeps Your Essentials Secure and Accessible

When preferring a leather wallet for travel, look for features that keep it safe and last a long time. Pick a wallet that has several sections to store your passport, travel documents, cards, and money securely. Traveling should be easy and durable. RFID protection is important to prevent digital theft. A zippered closure helps keep things in place while traveling.

For Business: A Professional and Functional Wallet

A business wallet should look superior and have enough space for storing credit cards, business cards, and cash. The design of your wallet should match your professional attire. The wallet is made of high-quality leather and has a minimalist design that shows your professional image.

Choosing the Right Leather Type

Synthetic Leather Vs Genuine Leather

Genuine leather is crafted from authentic animal hides and offers superior durability, breathability, and a distinctive texture that progressively improves with age. It usually needs more care and costs. Synthetic leather is convenient to maintain and easy to wipe clean. It offers a similar look at a lower price, but it may compromise on long-lasting quality.

Full-Grain Vs Top-Grain Leather

Full-grain leather is the best type of leather because it keeps the whole top layer. This makes it very durable and develops a rich patina over time. It is used in expensive products due to its natural imperfections and unique characteristics. Top-grain leather is less strong and has been treated to remove imperfections. This results in a uniform appearance and a softer feel. It also offers superior stain resistance and is typically less expensive than full-grain leather.

Evaluate the Features of a Leather Wallet Before Buying

  • The number of card slots is dependent on how many cards you currently have. There are more slots for better organization and a cleaner look.
  • Normal wallets have cash compartments for folks who carry bills and paperwork. However, simple wallets are smaller and have fewer pockets.
  • RFID technology prevents people from unauthorized scanning of your cards without your permission. Money is safe and secure with this.
  • Zipper closures keep your things safer because they fully cover them, while snap closures are easier to open but might not be as secure.
  • You can customize your wallet by selecting from a variety of designs, including unique initials or color options.

Selecting the Right Wallet Size and Design

Before Selecting the size and design think about how many cards, cash, and other items you typically carry with you every day. Choose a wallet that has enough pockets and slots to keep everything organized and fulfill your needs.

Also, consider factors such as size, material, design, security features, price, brand reputation, and personal preferences. At Kordovan, you'll find a wide range of wallets that you'll love and that will last for years.

Assessing Wallet Quality and Craftsmanship

Construction

When assessing wallet craftsmanship, pay close attention to the stitching and overall construction. A well-made wallet with strong, even stitches is less likely to break or show signs of wear, ensuring durability and longevity.

Durability

The material of your wallet affects its durability. A men's leather wallet made from high-quality material maintains its appearance and functionality over time.

Brand Reputation

Research the brand's reputation for quality and craftsmanship. Checking customer reviews and testimonials can provide insights into the wallet's performance and longevity.

Kordovan ensures their men's leather wallets are of high quality by using the finest responsibly sourced materials. Each wallet reflects their commitment to excellence.

Price Vs Value

Budget Friendly

If you're on a budget, there are many affordable leather wallet options available. Look for a small wallet made from durable materials that don't cost too much. At Kordovan, we offer an extensive range of smart, high-quality leather wallets that are budget-friendly.

Mid-Range

Mid-range wallets are crafted from genuine leather and are offered at reasonable prices. They fulfill basic needs and come with useful features such as RFID blocking and extra card slots.

Good Investment

Investing in high-quality wallets made from full-grain leather is worthwhile. These wallets, crafted from genuine leather, come with excellent features. While they may be more expensive than other options, but they offer a longer lifespan and a luxurious feel.

Top Recommendations for Kordovan Men's Leather Wallets

Kordovan range of leather wallets for men offers quality, style, and functionality at one place. These durable wallets are designed to last and cater to a variety of needs, making them a great choice for everyone. Kordovan leather wallets are great choices for those who want a mix of luxury and practicality.

You can choose from our best-selling wallets, which are customer favorites.

Shelby & Thomas: Bi-fold wallet

Soft milled leather is used to make the bi-fold Shelby & Thomas Wallet. There are two sides to this wallet, and it's available in black and brown colors. It's got a big cash pocket, perfect for keeping bills safe. It fits comfortably in your pocket because of the slimness of the wallet.

The Tango: RFID Wallet

nodes.body:
Updated September 2026 for the coming winter. Written by the Kordovan workshop team, where we have been cutting and stitching leather since 2019.

Read this first: we are on this list.

Kordovan makes leather jackets. Ranking ourselves is obviously self-serving, so we have tried to make the list useful anyway — every brand below gets an honest note on what it does well, we have said plainly where we are the wrong choice, and we have explained what a genuine leather jacket actually costs so you can judge any brand against it, including ours. If you only take one thing from this page, take the price section. It will save you more money than our discount codes will.

Here to buy rather than compare? Browse men's leather jackets in Pakistan — our own range, made to order from Rs 22,000.

Comparing another category? We have written the same kind of honest guide for each:

  • Best Winter Jackets in Pakistan — puffers, parkas and wool weighed against leather, by city
  • Top 10 Leather Wallet Brands in Pakistan
  • Best Leather Laptop and Office Bags in Pakistan
  • Top Leather Brands in Pakistan — every category in one place

The short version

Brand Best for Typical price band
Kordovan Genuine sheepskin, made to your size Rs 22,000 – 35,000
Jild Traditional construction, warranty Upper mid
Hub Established retail, easy returns Upper mid
Lawrencepur Classic, formal cuts Premium
Gul Ahmed Nationwide stores, exchanges Mid
Charcoal Modern, slim tailoring Mid to upper
Outfitters Trend-led styling, younger fits Entry to mid
The Black Birds Statement designs Entry to mid
The Ultimate Leather Men's and women's range Mid
Kaptan Hard-wearing, value Entry

Price bands are indicative and checked in August 2026. Every brand runs seasonal sales, so check the brand's own site before you decide. We have not published exact competitor prices because they change weekly and a stale number is worse than none.

What a genuine leather jacket actually costs in Pakistan

This is the part most lists skip, and it is the only part that protects you.

A finished genuine leather jacket needs roughly 25 to 35 square feet of hide. At Pakistani tannery rates for sheepskin or cowhide of a grade you would want against your skin, the leather alone runs well into five figures before anyone has cut a pattern, stitched a seam, fitted a lining, or paid for a YKK zip.

Which leads to a simple rule:

  • Under Rs 8,000 — almost certainly PU, rexine or a bonded-leather blend. It may look convincing on the hanger. It will crack and peel, usually within two winters.
  • Rs 8,000 – 15,000 — either a blend, a very small or thin hide, or a genuine jacket on heavy discount. Ask directly what the shell is made from and get the answer in writing.
  • Rs 20,000 – 40,000 — the honest band for a full genuine leather jacket made in Pakistan, properly lined and stitched.
  • Above Rs 45,000 — usually imported, or a designer margin. Not necessarily better leather.

None of this means an expensive jacket is automatically real. It means a cheap one almost certainly is not. If a seller will not tell you the hide and the finish, that is your answer.

How to check the leather yourself

Four tests you can do in a shop, in under a minute:

  1. Look at the pores. Real hide has an irregular grain — no two patches identical. PU repeats, because it is printed from a roll.
  2. Press it with your thumb. Genuine leather creases and springs back, and the colour shifts slightly as it stretches. Synthetic stays flat and uniform.
  3. Check the cut edges. Look inside a pocket or under the hem. Real leather has a fibrous, suede-like underside. PU shows a fabric mesh backing.
  4. Smell it. The least scientific and the hardest to fake. Leather smells of tannery. Synthetic smells faintly of plastic or chemical.

The ten brands

10. Kaptan

Built for hard wear rather than fashion. The cuts are simple and the range is narrow, but the construction is sturdy for the money. A reasonable first leather jacket if you want to find out whether you will actually wear one before spending more.

Watch out for: limited sizing and few style options.

9. The Ultimate Leather

One of the few Pakistani labels that treats women's leather as a real category rather than an afterthought. Stitching is tidy and the leather is honest for the price. Discounts appear often enough that it is worth waiting for one.

Watch out for: fit runs inconsistent between styles — check measurements rather than trusting the size label.

8. The Black Birds

The most design-forward name on this list. Hardware detailing, unusual panelling, jackets that are meant to be noticed. Popular with younger buyers for good reason.

Watch out for: statement pieces date faster than plain ones. If you want one jacket for ten years, this is not the shelf.

7. Lawrencepur

A long-established name with a formal, conservative eye. Their leather pieces sit closer to outerwear tailoring than to biker wear, which suits older buyers and office wardrobes.

Watch out for: priced at a premium, and the styling is deliberately unadventurous.

6. Charcoal

Modern, slim, well-finished. Charcoal understands proportion better than most of the mid-market, and their retail experience — sizing help, exchanges, service — is genuinely good.

Watch out for: slim cuts are unforgiving. Size up if you plan to wear a sweater underneath.

5. Jild

A leather specialist rather than a fashion house that added leather, and it shows in the construction. Traditional techniques, solid warranty, sensible range from classic to contemporary.

Watch out for: smaller retail footprint, so trying one on before buying can be difficult outside major cities.

4. Outfitters

The most accessible entry point. Wide reach, frequent sales, styling that tracks whatever is current. For a first jacket at a low price, it is a sensible place to start.

Watch out for: check the product description carefully. At the lower end of their range you are often looking at a blend rather than full grain.

3. Hub

Real leather, competent making, and the reassurance of an established retailer with straightforward returns. If buying online worries you, Hub removes most of that risk.

Watch out for: you pay something for that reassurance — the same construction costs less from a specialist.

2. Gul Ahmed

A textile house that moved into leather and brought its distribution with it. Stores in every major city, easy exchanges, dependable mid-market quality for men and women.

Watch out for: leather is a side line rather than the main event, so the range is narrower and turns over with the season.

1. Kordovan

We would say this, so here is the reasoning rather than the adjectives.

Every Kordovan jacket is cut from genuine sheepskin and made to order in our own workshop — we do not hold finished stock, so each one is built to your measurements rather than pulled from a size run. That is the whole argument: a leather jacket lives or dies on fit, and off-the-rack fit is a compromise for almost everyone.

The range covers biker, bomber, cafe racer and vintage cuts in black, brown, claret and blue, from Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000. Every piece carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty — if stitching or hardware fails in normal use, we repair or replace it.

How payment works: jackets are paid in full online at checkout — credit card, debit card or JazzCash. Cash on delivery is not offered on them. Each jacket is cut to your measurements and cannot be resold if it is refused at the door, so payment is what lets us start work.

Where we are the wrong choice, honestly:

  • You will wait. Made to order means production time, not next-day dispatch. If you need a jacket this weekend, we are not it.
  • You pay before we cut. If you will only pay at the door and nothing before, we are not set up for that — a made-to-measure jacket cannot be resold if it is refused.
  • No physical try-on outside our one shop. We have a single store in Malir Cantt. Everywhere else, you are working from a measurement chart.

Browse our men's leather jackets in Pakistan · women's leather jackets

Which style should you buy?

  • Biker — asymmetric zip, belted waist, the most structured option. Best over a t-shirt or thin knit. Reads casual, never formal.
  • Bomber — ribbed collar, cuffs and hem. The most forgiving cut and the easiest to wear with everything.
  • Cafe racer — minimal, band collar, centre zip. The closest leather gets to smart, and the one that works over a shirt.
  • Vintage / distressed — pre-aged finish. Looks broken-in immediately, and hides scuffs better than a clean finish does.

Buying for a Pakistani winter

Leather blocks wind extremely well and insulates poorly on its own. In the south, around Hyderabad and the coast, a lined jacket is enough on its own through most of the season. In Lahore, Islamabad, Rawalpindi and further north you want to layer underneath, which means allowing room in the chest when you choose a size. This is the single most common sizing mistake — buying a slim fit that fits perfectly over a t-shirt in September and will not close over a sweater in January.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best leather jacket brand in Pakistan?

It depends on what you are optimising for. For genuine leather made to your measurements, we would argue for Kordovan — though we are hardly neutral. For buying in person with easy exchanges, Gul Ahmed or Hub. For a low-priced first jacket, Outfitters. For traditional construction from a leather specialist, Jild.

How much should a genuine leather jacket cost in Pakistan?

Between roughly Rs 20,000 and Rs 40,000 for a full genuine leather jacket made locally. Below about Rs 8,000 you are almost certainly buying PU or a bonded blend, whatever the label says.

Is sheepskin better than cowhide for a jacket?

Different rather than better. Sheepskin is lighter, softer and drapes closer to the body — it is what most fashion leather jackets use. Cowhide is heavier and more abrasion-resistant, which is why motorcycle gear uses it. For everyday wear in Pakistan, sheepskin is usually the more comfortable choice.

How do I care for a leather jacket?

Keep it off wire hangers — use a broad wooden one so the shoulders hold. Never dry it on a radiator or in direct sun; let it air-dry away from heat. Condition it once or twice a year. Do not machine wash it, ever. Read our full leather care guide.

Are leather jackets worth it in Pakistan's climate?

For roughly four months of the year in the north and two to three in the south, yes. A genuine leather jacket lasts a decade or more with basic care, so the cost per wear works out lower than several synthetic jackets replaced every couple of seasons.

How can I tell if a jacket is real leather before buying online?

Ask the seller directly what the shell material is and get it in writing. Any honest brand will tell you the hide and the finish. Check the product page for the words "genuine", "full grain" or "sheepskin" rather than "leatherette", "PU" or simply "leather look". If a page avoids naming the material altogether, treat that as the answer.

The bottom line

Pakistan makes good leather. It also sells a great deal of plastic labelled as leather, and the gap between the two is not always visible on a product photo. Whichever brand you choose from this list, ask what the shell is made of, check the price against the bands above, and buy the jacket that fits — because a jacket that fits badly does not get worn, whatever it cost.

Ready to choose one? See our full range of men's leather jackets in Pakistan, made to order from Rs 22,000.

nodes.title: Top 10 Leather Wallet Brands in Pakistan (2026)
nodes.body:
Updated September 2026. Written by the Kordovan workshop team, where we cut and hand-stitch leather every day.

Read this first: we are on this list.

Kordovan makes leather wallets. Ranking ourselves is obviously self-serving, so we have tried to make the list useful anyway — every brand below gets an honest note on what it does well, we have said plainly where we are the wrong choice, and we have explained what a genuine leather wallet actually costs so you can judge any brand against it, including ours. If you only read one section, read the price one. It will save you more than any discount code.

Here to buy rather than compare? Browse men's leather wallets in Pakistan — hand-stitched in our own workshop from Rs 1,499.

The short version

Brand Best for Typical price band
Kordovan Full-grain and crazy horse, workshop pricing Rs 1,499 – 6,500
Jafferjees Heritage name, physical stores Premium
Hub Leather Mall retail, easy exchanges Mid
House of Leather Full-grain, waxed finishes Mid to upper
Jild Craft Leather specialist, classic shapes Mid
Blackbird Leathers Handmade, natural finishes Mid to upper
Uniworth Formal wardrobes, gifting sets Mid
Karar Online-first, slim everyday wallets Entry to mid
Eligo Leather Handmade, small-batch Entry to mid
Outfitters Trend-led styling, first wallet Entry

Price bands are indicative and checked in September 2026. Every brand runs seasonal sales, so check the brand's own site before you decide. We have deliberately not published exact competitor prices — they change weekly, and a stale number is worse than none.

What a genuine leather wallet actually costs in Pakistan

This is the part most lists skip, and it is the only part that protects you.

A bifold wallet takes roughly one and a half to two square feet of hide, plus lining, plus the labour of stitching a dozen card slots by hand or machine. The leather in a wallet is a small cost; the making is most of it. That leads to a simple set of bands:

  • Under Rs 800 — almost certainly PU, rexine or bonded leather. It will look convincing for a season, then crack along the fold. This is where most of the market sits.
  • Rs 800 – 1,500 — either a blend, a very thin split hide, or genuine leather on heavy discount. Ask what the outer material is and get the answer in writing.
  • Rs 1,500 – 7,000 — the honest band for a genuine leather wallet made in Pakistan, properly stitched and lined.
  • Above Rs 12,000 — usually an imported label or designer margin. Not necessarily better hide.

None of this means an expensive wallet is automatically real. It means a very cheap one almost certainly is not. If a seller will not name the hide and the finish, that is your answer.

How to check the leather yourself

Four tests, each takes seconds:

  1. Press it with your thumb. Genuine leather creases and springs back, and the colour shifts slightly as it stretches. PU stays flat and uniform.
  2. Look at the pores. Real hide has an irregular grain — no two patches identical. Synthetic repeats, because it is printed from a roll.
  3. Check inside a card slot. Real leather has a fibrous, suede-like underside at the cut edge. PU shows a woven fabric mesh backing.
  4. Look at the stitch. Even spacing, no loose ends, and the thread sitting down into the leather rather than on top of it. This is where cheap wallets fail first, long before the leather does.

The ten brands

10. Outfitters

The most accessible entry point, with wide mall presence and frequent sales. Styling follows whatever is current, which suits a first wallet you are not precious about.

Watch out for: read the material description carefully. At the lower end of the range you are usually looking at a synthetic or a blend rather than full grain.

9. Eligo Leather

A smaller online maker working in handmade batches, with a focus on plain, unfussy shapes. Worth a look if you want something made in small numbers rather than mass produced.

Watch out for: limited range and limited stock depth, so a specific colour may simply not be available when you want it.

8. Karar

Online-first and built around slim everyday carry rather than the traditional fat bifold. Clear product pages that name the leather, which is more than much of the market does.

Watch out for: slim wallets are a genuine trade-off. If you carry more than six or seven cards plus notes, measure before you commit.

7. Uniworth

A formalwear house that carries leather accessories alongside shirting and suiting, so the wallets are cut for a business wardrobe. Convenient if you are buying a gift set rather than a single piece.

Watch out for: leather is a side line rather than the main business, so the range is narrow and turns over with the season.

6. Blackbird Leathers

Handmade wallets in natural, lightly finished leathers that are meant to darken with use. If you like a wallet that looks visibly different after a year, this is the right shelf.

Watch out for: natural finishes mark easily at the start. That is the point of them, but it surprises people who wanted it to stay pristine.

5. Jild Craft

A leather specialist rather than a fashion label that added leather, and the construction shows it. Classic bifold and trifold shapes, sensibly priced, with clear material descriptions.

Watch out for: deliberately conservative styling. Nothing here is going to be the most interesting object in your pocket.

4. House of Leather

Full-grain cowhide with waxed and pull-up finishes, aimed at buyers who want a wallet with visible character rather than a flat uniform surface. Good detail on materials in their listings.

Watch out for: pull-up leather shows every scratch as a lighter mark. Most people grow to like it; some do not.

3. Hub Leather

Well distributed through malls across the country, with the reassurance of walking in, handling the wallet and exchanging it if it is wrong. For anyone nervous about buying leather online, that removes most of the risk.

Watch out for: you pay something for that convenience. Comparable construction usually costs less from a specialist making the same thing.

2. Jafferjees

The oldest name in Pakistani leather goods and still the benchmark for heritage. Solidly made, conservatively designed, and available in person in the major cities. If you want a wallet from a house that has been doing this longer than anyone else here, this is it.

Watch out for: priced at the top of the local market, and the designs are deliberately traditional.

1. Kordovan

We would say this, so here is the reasoning rather than the adjectives.

We cut and stitch every wallet in our own workshop in Malir Cantt, in full-grain, nappa, crazy horse and saffiano leathers. Because there is no importer and no middle layer between the bench and the box, a full-grain wallet starts at Rs 1,499 and the most expensive thing we make is Rs 6,500.

The range runs from slim card holders and money clips through classic bifolds to long wallets and RFID smart wallets. Every piece carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty — if stitching or hardware fails in normal use, we repair or replace it.

Wallets are ready-made and dispatched from stock, so cash on delivery is available, along with card and JazzCash. Free delivery over Rs 5,500.

Where we are the wrong choice, honestly:

  • You want to hold it first. We have only one physical shop. Everywhere else you are buying from photographs and a description.
  • You want a designer label. We do not put a large logo on the outside, and for some buyers that is the entire point of the purchase.
  • You want it in a specific colour today. We make in batches. Popular colours do sell out, and a restock takes weeks rather than days.

Browse men's leather wallets · women's wallets · RFID smart wallets

Which wallet shape should you buy?

  • Bifold — the default. Folds once, holds notes flat and six to twelve cards. If you are not sure, buy this.
  • Trifold — more card slots in a shorter body, but noticeably thicker in the pocket. Good if you carry a lot of cards and do not sit on your wallet.
  • Card holder / money clip — the slimmest option. Four to eight cards and folded notes. Front-pocket carry.
  • Long wallet — notes unfolded, full-size documents, often a zip. Carried in a jacket or bag rather than a trouser pocket.
  • RFID smart wallet — a slim body with shielding built in, for contactless cards. Pull-tab or fan mechanisms rather than slots.

What actually makes a wallet last

In order of how often we see them fail:

  1. The stitch at the fold. This takes the most stress and it is where cheap wallets split first. Look for tight, even stitching that sits down into the leather.
  2. The card slots. Slots stretch with use. A slot with a reinforced or bound edge holds its shape years longer than a raw cut one.
  3. The lining. A fabric lining wears through from the inside while the outside still looks new. Leather-lined or leather-backed slots cost more and outlast it.
  4. The leather itself. Genuinely last on the list. Full grain outlives everything else in the wallet.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best leather wallet brand in Pakistan?

It depends what you are optimising for. For full-grain leather at a workshop price, we would argue for Kordovan — though we are hardly neutral. For heritage and a physical store to walk into, Jafferjees. For buying in a mall with easy exchanges, Hub. For a first wallet at a low price, Outfitters.

How much should a genuine leather wallet cost in Pakistan?

Roughly Rs 1,500 to Rs 6,500 for a genuine leather wallet made locally. Below about Rs 800 you are almost certainly buying PU or bonded leather, whatever the label says. Above Rs 12,000 you are usually paying for an imported label rather than better hide.

Is full-grain or top-grain leather better for a wallet?

Full grain keeps the outermost layer of the hide with its natural markings, so it is the strongest and it develops a patina. Top grain is sanded to remove blemishes, which makes it more uniform but slightly less durable. For a wallet that gets opened thousands of times a year, full grain is the better buy.

Do I need an RFID wallet in Pakistan?

Only if you carry contactless cards. RFID shielding blocks the radio handshake a contactless card uses, which prevents skimming. If your cards are chip-and-PIN with no contactless symbol, the feature does nothing for you. It costs little to include, so take it when it is offered rather than paying a large premium for it.

How long should a leather wallet last?

A genuine leather wallet used daily should last five to ten years, and full grain often longer. What fails first is usually the stitching at the fold and the card slots, not the leather — which is why stitch quality deserves more of your attention than the brand name.

How do I tell a real leather wallet from a fake one?

Press the surface with your thumb: real leather creases and springs back and the colour shifts as it stretches, while PU stays flat. Look at the pores — irregular on real hide, repeating on printed synthetic. Check the cut edge inside a card slot for a fibrous, suede-like underside rather than a fabric mesh backing. Our leather guide goes into more detail.

The bottom line

Pakistan makes very good leather, and it also sells a great deal of plastic labelled as leather. On a wallet the gap is easy to spot once you know what to press and where to look. Whichever brand you choose from this list, ask what the outer material is, check the price against the bands above, and pay more attention to the stitching than to the logo — because the stitching is what will fail first.

Ready to choose one? See our full range of leather wallets for men in Pakistan, hand-stitched in our own workshop from Rs 1,499. Also worth reading: Top 10 Leather Jacket Brands in Pakistan.

nodes.title: Best Winter Jackets in Pakistan (2026): Types, Brands and Real Prices
nodes.body:
Updated September 2026 for the coming winter. Written by the Kordovan workshop team.

Read this first: we make one kind of jacket, not all of them.

Kordovan makes leather jackets. We do not make puffers, parkas or wool coats — so for most of this guide we have no stake in what you choose, and we have tried to be straight about when leather is the wrong answer. It often is. If you live in Murree and need to be warm in January, a leather jacket is not what you want, and we will say so below.

The short version

Type Best for Realistic price
Puffer Everyday warmth, most Pakistani cities Rs 3,000 – 8,000
Parka Northern areas, wet or genuinely cold Rs 8,000 – 20,000
Wool / overcoat Formal wear, offices, weddings Rs 8,000 – 25,000
Leather Wind, style, lasting a decade Rs 20,000 – 40,000
Fleece / softshell Layering, mild winters, travel Rs 2,500 – 6,000
Denim / cotton Autumn only, not real winter Rs 2,000 – 5,000

Start with where you live, not with the jacket

Pakistan does not have one winter, it has about four. Buying for the wrong one is the most expensive mistake in this category — and it is usually a jacket that is too warm to wear rather than too thin.

  • The south: Hyderabad and the coast. A handful of genuinely cool weeks. A light padded jacket, a fleece or a lined leather jacket covers the entire season. A heavy puffer will sit in a cupboard.
  • Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan, Gujranwala. Cold mornings and evenings from December to February, mild afternoons. A mid-weight puffer, or a leather jacket over a sweater, handles almost everything.
  • Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Sialkot. Colder and damper. A puffer with real fill weight, or a parka if you are outdoors early and late.
  • Murree, Swat, Quetta, Gilgit and the north. Actual winter. A hooded, insulated parka. Nothing on this page except a proper parka is enough on its own.

How much fill you actually need

Fill weight is the number that decides whether a puffer works, and almost nobody publishes it. If a listing does not state the fill, ask.

  • Under 100g — an autumn jacket. Fine for October, not for January anywhere north of the coast.
  • 150–250g synthetic — the sweet spot for most of Pakistan. Warm enough for a Lahore or Islamabad winter, not so warm that you stop wearing it indoors.
  • 300g and above — northern areas and genuine cold. You will overheat in it in most cities.

Down fill is warmer per gram than synthetic and packs smaller, but it loses most of its insulation when wet and costs considerably more. For Pakistani conditions, good synthetic fill is usually the more sensible buy.

What a winter jacket actually costs here

The bands that matter, whatever the label says:

  • Under Rs 2,000 — thin fill in a thin shell. It will look right for one season and flatten by the second. This is the bulk of what is sold online.
  • Rs 3,000 – 8,000 — the honest band for a synthetic puffer that lasts three to five winters with real fill weight behind it.
  • Rs 8,000 – 20,000 — a proper parka, a wool overcoat, or a well-made technical jacket.
  • Rs 20,000 – 40,000 — genuine leather. A different purchase entirely: you are buying ten years, not one winter.

Where to buy: the brands worth knowing

Brand Strongest at Band
Outfitters Puffers and casual winter, frequent sales Entry to mid
Breakout Younger fits, wide colour range Entry
Cougar Broad jacket range including suede and puffer Entry to mid
Gul Ahmed / Ideas Nationwide stores, easy exchanges Mid
Bonanza Satrangi Knitwear and quilted, family sizing Entry to mid
Uniworth / Diners Formal overcoats and office winter Mid to upper
Charcoal Slim modern tailoring Mid to upper
Kordovan Genuine leather, made to your measurements Rs 22,000 – 35,000

Bands are indicative and checked in September 2026. We have not published exact competitor prices — they change with every sale, and a stale number is worse than none.

Where leather fits, honestly

Leather is the best windproof layer money can buy and one of the worst insulators. That single sentence explains most of what people get wrong about it.

Leather is the right answer if: you are in Lahore, Multan or the south, you want one jacket that will still look good in ten years, and you are happy to put a sweater underneath on the coldest nights.

Leather is the wrong answer if: you need to be warm standing still in Murree in January, you want something you can machine wash, or you want to spend under Rs 15,000. A genuine leather jacket does not exist below roughly Rs 20,000 in Pakistan, and anything cheaper claiming to be one is almost always PU.

We cover the leather side properly in a separate guide: Top 10 Leather Jacket Brands in Pakistan, including how to tell real hide from plastic before you pay.

Our own jackets are cut from genuine sheepskin and made to order in our own workshop, from Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000, with a lifetime craftsmanship warranty. They are paid in full online at checkout, because each one is cut to a single customer's measurements and cannot be resold if it is refused at the door. Allow about three weeks from checkout to your door — winter is our busiest season and the bench is full.

Browse men's leather jackets · women's leather jackets

The sizing mistake almost everyone makes

You try the jacket on in September, over a t-shirt. It fits beautifully. In January you put a sweater on underneath and it will not close.

Buy for the layer you will actually be wearing in the coldest month. On a puffer, allow room to get a fist between your chest and the closed zip. On leather, which does not stretch back once it has stretched, size for the sweater rather than the shirt. If you are between sizes and the jacket is your main winter layer, take the larger one.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best winter jacket for Pakistan?

It depends where you live. In the south, around Hyderabad and the coast, a light padded jacket or a lined leather jacket is enough for the whole season. In Lahore, Islamabad and Rawalpindi a puffer with 150 to 250 grams of fill covers most nights. For Murree, Swat, Skardu or Quetta in deep winter you want a proper insulated parka with a hood.

How much should a good winter jacket cost in Pakistan?

Roughly Rs 3,000 to Rs 8,000 for a decent synthetic puffer, Rs 8,000 to Rs 20,000 for a well-made parka or wool coat, and Rs 20,000 to Rs 40,000 for a genuine leather jacket. Below about Rs 2,000 you are buying thin fill in a shell that will not survive two seasons.

Is a leather jacket warm enough for Pakistani winter?

Leather blocks wind extremely well but insulates poorly by itself. A lined leather jacket is comfortable on its own through a mild southern winter. Further north it works as a windproof outer layer over a sweater rather than as your only source of warmth.

Puffer or parka, which is better?

A puffer is shorter, lighter and easier to wear every day. A parka is longer, usually hooded, and covers the hips, which matters when it is genuinely cold or wet. For most Pakistani cities a puffer is enough; for the northern areas in December and January a parka earns its bulk.

What fill weight do I need?

For most of the country, 150 to 250 grams of synthetic fill covers the season. Below 100 grams is an autumn jacket. Above 300 grams you will overheat anywhere except the northern mountains in deep winter.

What size should I buy?

Size for the layer you will wear underneath in January, not the t-shirt you have on when you try it in September. That is the single most common winter jacket mistake.

The bottom line

Decide where you will actually wear it before you decide what it is made of. For most Pakistani cities a mid-weight puffer at Rs 3,000 to 8,000 does the job for three to five winters. For the north, buy the parka. And if you want one jacket that outlasts all of them and looks better every year, that is where leather earns its price — as long as you accept that it is a windbreaker with style, not a source of warmth on its own.

Looking specifically at leather? Read Top 10 Leather Jacket Brands in Pakistan, or browse our made-to-order leather jackets from Rs 22,000.

Read this first: we are on this list.

We have tried to make the page useful anyway: every brand gets an honest note, we say where we are the wrong choice, and the price section applies to every name here including ours. If you read one part, read that one — it is what tells you whether a price makes sense before you pay it.

Why Pakistan makes good leather

This matters, because the most common assumption we hear is that imported means better.

Pakistan has one of the older tanning industries in the region. Kasur, south of Lahore, has been a tanning centre for generations. Sialkot is known worldwide for leather goods and gloves. The port cities hold a dense cluster of leather goods workshops and exporters. A significant share of finished leather and leather goods made here is exported and sold under other labels abroad.

Which means the raw material available to a Pakistani brand is genuinely good. The variation you see between shops is almost never about the country — it is about which grade of hide a brand chooses to buy, and how carefully the thing is stitched. Two wallets from the same tannery can be five years apart in lifespan depending on who made them.

What genuine leather actually costs in Pakistan

Every category has a floor below which the maths does not work. Learn these and you can judge any brand, including ours.

Item Almost certainly synthetic below Honest band for genuine
Wallet Rs 800 Rs 1,500 – 7,000
Belt Rs 1,000 Rs 2,000 – 6,000
Laptop / office bag Rs 5,000 Rs 12,000 – 45,000
Formal shoes Rs 4,000 Rs 8,000 – 30,000
Jacket Rs 8,000 Rs 20,000 – 40,000

An expensive item is not automatically real. But a very cheap one almost certainly is not, because the hide alone costs more than the asking price. If a seller will not name the material and the finish in writing, treat that as the answer.

Full grain, top grain, genuine, bonded

These words are not interchangeable, and one of them is actively misleading.

  • Full grain — the outermost layer of the hide, surface intact, natural markings visible. Strongest, and the only grade that develops a real patina.
  • Top grain — the same layer sanded to remove blemishes, then finished. More uniform, slightly less durable, still a good buy.
  • "Genuine leather" — a grade, not a compliment. Usually the lower splits of the hide after the good layers are taken off. It is real leather and it is the weakest kind.
  • Bonded leather — leather scrap ground up and glued to a backing. Avoid. It fails like plastic because it mostly is.

How to check, in under a minute

  1. Thumb press. Real leather creases and springs back, and the tone shifts as it stretches. Synthetic stays flat and uniform.
  2. Pores. Irregular on real hide, no two patches alike. Printed PU repeats, because it comes off a roll.
  3. Cut edge. Look inside a pocket or under a hem. Real leather is fibrous and suede-like underneath. PU shows a woven mesh backing.
  4. Smell. Least scientific, hardest to fake. Leather smells of tannery; synthetic smells faintly of plastic.

Buying by category

Brand reputation rarely transfers across categories — a house that makes excellent bags is not automatically good at shoes. We have written separate guides for the categories where the differences matter most:

  • Top 10 Leather Wallet Brands in Pakistan — what a real wallet costs, and why stitching fails before leather does.
  • Top 10 Leather Jacket Brands in Pakistan — sheepskin versus cowhide, and the price floor for a genuine jacket.
  • Best Leather Laptop and Office Bags in Pakistan — what actually protects a laptop, and why hardware matters more than hide.
  • Best Winter Jackets in Pakistan — where leather fits against puffers and parkas, by city.

Where we fit, and where we do not

Kordovan cuts and stitches in our own workshop in Malir Cantt. Wallets and small leather goods start at Rs 1,499; laptop and office bags run Rs 8,500 to Rs 42,000; made-to-order jackets are Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000. Everything carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty against stitching and hardware failure in normal use.

Ready-made pieces — wallets, bags, belts, hats and accessories — can be bought cash on delivery. Jackets and footwear are made to order and paid online at checkout, because each one is cut to a single customer's measurements and cannot be resold if it is refused at the door.

Where we are the wrong choice:

  • You want to handle it first. We have one shop. Everywhere else you are buying from photographs.
  • You want a visible designer logo. We do not put one on the outside.
  • You want a jacket this week. Made to order means about three weeks, and longer in peak winter.

Browse wallets · bags · jackets · belts · shoes

Frequently asked questions

Which is the best leather brand in Pakistan?

There is no single answer across categories. Jafferjees is the heritage benchmark for bags and formal goods. Hub is the easiest to buy in person. Kordovan — ours — makes wallets, bags and made-to-order jackets from our own workshop. For shoes, English Boot House and Servis dominate different ends of the market. Pick by category rather than by brand name.

Is Pakistani leather good quality?

Pakistan has a long-established tanning industry centred on Kasur and Sialkot, and it exports leather and finished goods worldwide. The raw material is genuinely good. The variation you see in shops is mostly about which grade a brand buys and how well it is stitched, not about the country.

How can I tell genuine leather from fake?

Press it with your thumb — real leather creases and springs back and the colour shifts as it stretches, while synthetic stays flat. Look at the pores: irregular on real hide, repeating on printed PU. Check a cut edge for a fibrous, suede-like underside rather than a woven fabric backing. And check the price against the bands above.

What is the difference between full grain and "genuine leather"?

Confusingly, "genuine leather" is a grade rather than a guarantee — usually the lower splits of the hide, and the weakest real leather you can buy. Full grain is the top layer with its surface intact and is the strongest. Bonded leather is scrap glued to a backing and should be avoided entirely.

Where is leather made in Pakistan?

Kasur near Lahore is the historic tanning centre, Sialkot is known for leather goods and gloves, and the coast holds a large concentration of leather workshops and exporters. Most consumer brands source their hide from these clusters whether they say so or not.

The bottom line

Pakistan makes leather good enough to export to countries that put their own labels on it. It also sells a very large amount of plastic described as leather, and the words on the label will not tell you which is which. Learn the price floors, learn the thumb press, and buy from whoever will tell you in writing what the material is — that single test eliminates most of the market, and it works on us too.

nodes.body:
Updated September 2026. Written by the Kordovan workshop team, where we make these.

Read this first: we are on this list.

Kordovan makes leather laptop and office bags, so we are not neutral. What we can do is tell you what actually determines whether one of these survives five years of daily carry — and it is not the thing most listings talk about. Read the "what fails first" section even if you buy from someone else. It is the part that will save you money.

Here to buy rather than compare? Browse leather laptop bags in Pakistan — made in our own workshop from Rs 8,500.

The short version

Brand Best for Typical price band
Kordovan Full range, sleeves through executive briefcases Rs 8,500 – 42,000
Jafferjees Formal briefcases, heritage name Premium
House of Leather Full-grain waxed finishes, patina Mid to upper
Hub Leather Buying in person, easy exchanges Mid
Blackbird Leathers Handmade, natural finishes Mid to upper
Uniworth Corporate gifting, formal sets Mid
Outfitters / Breakout Entry price, mostly synthetic Entry

Bands are indicative and checked in September 2026. We have not published exact competitor prices — they change with every sale, and a stale number is worse than none.

A note on search results. Search "leather laptop bag manufacturer Pakistan" and most of what comes back is business-to-business exporters selling by the container, not shops that will send you one bag. They are legitimate companies and irrelevant to a single purchase. If a site quotes MOQ, minimum order quantity, it is not selling to you.

What a genuine leather laptop bag costs here

A laptop bag takes far more hide than a wallet — a full briefcase uses roughly ten to fifteen square feet, plus lining, padding, a frame in some designs, and a good deal of hardware. The bands follow from that:

  • Under Rs 5,000 — PU or bonded, effectively always. There is no version of this maths where a genuine leather laptop bag is made and sold for less.
  • Rs 8,000 – 12,000 — a genuine leather sleeve is realistic here. A full structured bag at this price is not.
  • Rs 12,000 – 45,000 — the honest band for a genuine leather laptop bag or office briefcase made in Pakistan.
  • Above Rs 60,000 — imported labels and designer margin. Rarely better hide than the band below it.

What actually fails first

We repair these under warranty, so this list is from the repair bench rather than from a spec sheet. In order:

  1. The zip. Not close. A cheap zip on a bag that is opened four times a day will fail inside two years, and it usually takes the bag with it because replacing a full-length zip costs more than most people will pay. Look for a branded zip, or at minimum a heavy metal tooth rather than moulded plastic.
  2. The strap attachment points. Where D-rings and clips meet the leather is where all the load concentrates. Reinforced, riveted or double-stitched anchors last; a single line of stitching through one layer does not.
  3. The base corners. A bag gets put down on concrete, thousands of times. Corners that are reinforced or have metal feet survive; unprotected corners wear through to the lining.
  4. The lining. Fails invisibly from the inside while the outside still looks new. This is why a cheap bag can look fine and be useless.
  5. The leather. Genuinely last. Full-grain hide outlives every component attached to it.

The uncomfortable conclusion is that the grade of leather — the thing every product page leads with — is close to the least important factor in how long your bag lasts. Judge the metalwork first.

What actually protects your laptop

Leather is abrasion resistant. It is not shock absorbing. A laptop in an unpadded leather bag is a laptop resting against a hard flat panel, and when you set the bag down firmly the machine takes that impact.

What you want is a padded compartment that is suspended — one that holds the laptop clear of the bottom of the bag rather than sitting flush against it. That two-centimetre gap is the single most protective feature in any laptop bag at any price, and plenty of expensive bags do not have it. If a listing does not show the inside of the laptop compartment, ask for a photograph.

Briefcase, messenger, backpack or sleeve?

  • Briefcase — the most formal, structured, and the one that looks right in a boardroom. Also the most awkward to carry on a motorcycle and the hardest on one shoulder. Best if you drive to work.
  • Messenger — a flap and a cross-body strap. Faster to get into than a briefcase, comfortable one-handed, less formal. The most practical choice for most people who commute.
  • Backpack — the only sensible option above about four kilograms. Laptop plus charger plus files plus a water bottle crosses that line quickly, and a backpack is what saves your shoulder.
  • Sleeve — no carry handle, goes inside another bag. The cheapest way to add real protection to a laptop you are already carrying in something else.

Sizing: measure the machine, not the screen

Screen size is a diagonal measurement and tells you almost nothing about whether a laptop fits. Two machines both described as fifteen inch can differ by more than two centimetres in width depending on bezel and body.

Measure your laptop's actual width and depth, then allow roughly two centimetres in each direction for padding and the sleeve wall. A compartment that fits your machine exactly is one you will struggle with every single morning.

The Kordovan range

We make these in our own workshop in Malir Cantt, in full-grain, natural milled and crazy horse leathers. The range runs from Rs 8,500 for a laptop sleeve, through slim messengers and office bags in the twenties, up to Rs 42,000 for the executive briefcases. Every piece carries a lifetime craftsmanship warranty covering stitching and hardware in normal use — which is precisely the list above.

Bags are ready-made and dispatched from stock, so cash on delivery is available alongside card and JazzCash. Free delivery over Rs 5,500.

Where we are the wrong choice, honestly:

  • You want to try the fit with your own laptop first. Only our one shop lets you do that. Everywhere else, measure carefully and check the stated compartment size.
  • You need it waterproof. Leather is water resistant, not waterproof. If you ride a bike through monsoon rain daily, buy technical nylon and keep the leather for the office.
  • You want the lightest possible bag. Leather weighs more than nylon. An empty full-grain briefcase is a real object before you put anything in it.

Browse laptop bags · office bags and briefcases · leather backpacks · all bags

Frequently asked questions

How much does a genuine leather laptop bag cost in Pakistan?

Roughly Rs 12,000 to Rs 45,000 for a genuine leather laptop bag or briefcase made locally. A leather sleeve without full bag structure starts lower, around Rs 8,000. Below about Rs 5,000 you are almost certainly buying PU or a bonded blend.

What size laptop bag do I need?

Measure your laptop's width and depth rather than trusting the screen size — a 14 inch machine can be physically larger than a 15 inch one. Then allow about two centimetres in each direction for padding.

Is a leather bag actually good for carrying a laptop?

Leather is abrasion resistant and outlasts nylon by years, but leather alone does not protect against a drop. What protects a laptop is a padded compartment that holds it clear of the bottom of the bag. Check for that before you check the hide.

Briefcase, messenger or backpack for the office?

A briefcase is the most formal and the most awkward on a bike. A messenger is quicker to get into and easier one-handed. A backpack spreads weight across both shoulders and is the only sensible option above about four kilograms — which laptop plus charger plus files reaches quickly.

What fails first on a leather laptop bag?

The zip, almost always. Then the strap attachment points where hardware meets leather. The hide itself is rarely the problem, which is why the metalwork deserves more attention than the grade of leather.

Can I buy a leather office bag on cash on delivery?

Most Pakistani leather retailers including us offer cash on delivery on ready-made bags. Confirm before ordering, since made-to-order pieces are usually paid online — they cannot be resold if refused at the door.

The bottom line

Buy the bag that fits your laptop with room to spare, check the zip before you check the leather, and look for a suspended padded compartment rather than a flat pocket. Get those three right and almost any genuine leather bag in the Rs 12,000 to 45,000 band will still be working in five years. Get them wrong and the grade of hide will not save you.

Ready to choose one? See our leather laptop bags and office briefcases, made in our own workshop from Rs 8,500. Also worth reading: Top Leather Brands in Pakistan.

nodes.title: Real vs Fake Leather: 8 Ways to Check Before You Buy
nodes.body:
Updated October 2026. Written by the Kordovan workshop team.

Rexine and PU are often sold as leather in Pakistan, sometimes at leather prices. In a shop you can usually tell the difference in under a minute once you know where to look. Online it is harder, so this guide covers both: eight checks you can do with the piece in your hands, and what to look for on a product page before you order.

We sell leather goods. Kordovan makes wallets, jackets, bags and belts, so we have an interest in this topic. Every test below works on any brand, ours included, and none of them needs special tools.

The short answer

Look at the cut edge and the back. Real leather shows tightly packed fibres on the edge and a fuzzy, suede-like underside. Rexine and PU show a thin shiny layer stuck onto woven fabric or mesh. If you can only do one check, do this one.

Leather, PU and rexine: what each one actually is

Material What it is How it ages
Real leather Animal hide (usually cow, buffalo, sheep or goat) that has been tanned so it does not rot. Softens, darkens and picks up a patina. A good piece lasts many years with basic care.
PU leather Fabric coated with polyurethane and pressed with a leather-like grain. Looks fine at first, then cracks and peels, often within a year or two of regular use.
Rexine The local name for fabric coated with PVC (sometimes PU). Common on car seats, sofas and cheap jackets. Stiff, does not breathe, and peels at folds and edges.

"Vegan leather" and "faux leather" are usually PU. Some brands sell them openly, which is fine. The problem is only when they are sold as leather.

Grades of real leather, in plain words

  • Full-grain: the top layer of the hide with its natural surface left on. The strongest grade, and the one that ages best.
  • Top-grain: the top layer with the surface lightly sanded or finished for an even look. Slightly softer and more uniform. Most good leather jackets use it.
  • Split and suede: the lower layers of the hide. Suede is a split with a brushed, napped finish. Real leather, but weaker than the top layers.
  • Bonded leather: leftover scraps ground up and glued onto a backing. It contains some leather but behaves like PU and peels the same way.

One label trap: abroad, "genuine leather" is sometimes printed on lower grades. In Pakistan sellers use it to mean "real". Ask which grade it is, or check the product page.

8 ways to check if leather is real

1. Look at the cut edge

Find an unfinished edge, inside a card slot, at a seam, or where a strap ends. Real leather shows a dense layer of fibres, a bit like the edge of thick cardboard. PU and rexine show a thin plastic layer on top of fabric threads, and sometimes you can see the two layers separating.

2. Check the back side

Turn the piece over or look under the lining. The underside of real leather is fibrous and slightly fuzzy, like suede. A woven or knitted fabric backing means it is coated fabric.

3. Look closely at the surface

Real hide has pores and grain that vary across the piece, with the odd small scar or crease. Fake leather has a pressed pattern that repeats perfectly. If two areas look identical, be suspicious.

4. Press and bend it

Press a fingertip into the surface or fold a corner. Real leather forms fine wrinkles that soften away when you let go, and the colour can lighten slightly at the fold. PU and rexine dent without wrinkling, or form a hard crease that stays.

5. Smell it

Real leather has a warm, earthy smell. Fake leather smells of plastic or chemicals, or of nothing at all. Heavy perfume or polish can hide the smell, so do not rely on this check alone.

6. Feel the temperature

Hold it for a minute. Real leather warms up to your hand and feels slightly soft. Rexine stays cool and smooth, a bit like plastic.

7. The water drop test

Put one small drop of water on a hidden spot. Uncoated leather absorbs it slowly and darkens for a moment before drying. Coated fabric lets the drop sit on top. Some real leathers are finished or waxed and will also make the drop bead, so a bead alone does not prove it is fake. Wipe it off straight away.

8. The lighter test (only on something you already own)

This is the test most people in Pakistan have heard of. Pass a lighter flame under an edge for a second or two, keeping it moving. Real leather may char slightly and smells like burnt hair. PU and rexine melt, bubble or shrink and smell of burning plastic.

Be careful with it. A flame can leave a mark even on real leather, and a shop will not thank you for testing their stock. Use it only on a hidden spot of something you have already bought, and only if the other checks left you unsure.

How to check before you buy online

  • Read the material line. A real leather product names the hide and grade, for example "top-grain sheep leather". Vague wording such as "premium leather look" or "leather finish" usually means PU.
  • Zoom into the photos. Look for an edge or the inside of a pocket. Sellers of real leather tend to show it; sellers of PU tend to show only the shiny front.
  • Check the price. Hide, tanning and stitching cost money. A full leather jacket for a few thousand rupees, or a "leather" wallet cheaper than a meal out, deserves a second look.
  • Read the warranty and returns. A brand confident in its leather usually backs it with a warranty and a clear returns policy.
  • Ask the seller directly. Ask what animal and which grade. A straight answer is a good sign. "100% original sir" with no detail is not.

What real leather costs in Pakistan

We will not quote other brands' prices, because they change often and a wrong number is worse than none. For reference, here is our own range for real leather:

  • Leather wallets: Rs 1,499 to Rs 6,500
  • Leather jackets: Rs 22,000 to Rs 35,000, made to order in top-grain sheep leather

Cheaper real leather exists, especially in smaller items and lower grades. But when a jacket is priced like a fabric jacket, the material is the first thing to question.

Where Kordovan fits

Every product page on our site names the leather it is made from. Our jackets are top-grain sheep leather, cut and stitched to order in our own workshop. Each product page also states its warranty, and most of our leather pieces carry a lifetime craftsmanship warranty.

We also sell two bags that are not leather, and we say so in the name: The Diva Tote // Vegan and The Vibe // LITE // Vegan. If you want leather, skip those two. If you prefer to avoid animal products, they are the ones for you.

If you want to compare brands side by side, see our guide to leather brands in Pakistan. Once you own a leather piece, our leather care guide explains how to keep it in good shape.

Frequently asked questions

Is "genuine leather" real leather?

Yes, it is made from hide. Outside Pakistan the phrase is sometimes used for lower grades, so ask whether it is full-grain, top-grain or split.

Is PU leather real leather?

No. PU leather is fabric coated with polyurethane. It is cheaper and can look good at first, but it does not age like leather and usually peels with time.

What is rexine?

Rexine is fabric coated with PVC or PU and embossed to look like leather. It is common on car seats, furniture and low-priced jackets.

Does real leather crack or peel?

Real leather can dry out and crack if it is never cleaned or conditioned, but it does not peel in flakes. Peeling is a sign of a coating on fabric, which means PU, rexine or bonded leather.

Which test is the most reliable?

The cut edge and the back side. They show what the material is made of, and they do not damage anything.

Is the lighter test safe?

It can mark the surface even on real leather. Only use it on a hidden spot of something you own, and only if the other checks were not clear.

Bottom line

Check the edge and the back first, then the surface and the feel. Use water or a flame only when the easy checks leave you unsure. And when you buy online, choose a seller who names the leather and puts a warranty behind it.
